text:
Alex: Noticing a sharp 95th/99th latency spike on prod after the 03:10 kernel-selection rollout. Dashboards look off though — the request count graph drops at the same time which doesn't match what users reported.

InfraBot: Deploy event: rollout/ksel-v2 -> started 1938001200, finished 1938001226 (canary -> step1). No automatic rollback triggered.

Alex: Copied a short trace from a slow request (no full spans): `trace_id=0x8f3a...` — shows token generation stalling at kernel selection. But most traces missing.

Maria: I see the same. Traces for a subset of hosts are absent between 1938001228-1938001360. Sampling rate on those hosts is 0.01 in config; wasn't changed in the rollout. Dashboard annotations show the rollout, but traces are sparse.

Sam: Two quick guesses: (1) the kernel selector added a fast-path that bails without emitting the usual span, (2) the profiler sampling was accidentally lowered in the canary image. Both would explain missing spans + perf change.

Jane: Also seeing KV cache eviction rate jump 3x on the same hosts at 1938001230. Could be noisy-neighbor eviction causing more cold starts -> higher latency. Correlation looks strong.

Alex: Can someone pull a quick flamegraph sample from host gpu-12-3? I want pprof profiles from the 1938001240 window.

Priya: Oncall -> running remote pprof now, setting trace sampling to 100% for hosts in pool=prod-ksel. Will post results.

InfraBot: Command executed by Priya: `set-trace-sampling --pool prod-ksel --rate 1.0` -> success.

Sam: While that's running, check the kernel-selection flags in the rollout bundle. There's a config flag `selector.fast_path_pref` that was bumped to 0.9 in the canary. If fast path drops span emission, that's a bug.

Maria: FYI — alerted that Prometheus scrape on prometheus-scrape-2 failed between 1938001260-1938001300, which explains the request-count hole on the dashboard. The underlying metrics existed on the nodes but didn't make it to the central TSDB.

Alex: Ok that explains the dashboard mismatch. So two independent issues: (A) missing traces due to low sampling + selector fast-path skipping spans, (B) KV eviction/noisy neighbor causing higher per-request work. Both amplified the user-visible latency.

Jane: I pulled the eviction logs: `/var/log/runtime/kv-evict.log` snippet: ```[1938001231] evict pool=prod-ksel key_count=4521 freed=112 policy=LRU``` repeated rapidly. Also host-level GPU utilization shows another tenant hitting sustained 98% on gpu-12-3 around the same window.

Sam: Suggested immediate mitigations: (1) rollback fast_path_pref to 0.6 on canary and pause rollout, (2) bump sample rate to 100% for affected hosts (done), (3) pin noisy tenant to different GPU pool if possible.

Priya: Rolled back selector flag in the canary and paused rollout at 1938001345. InfraBot confirmed.

InfraBot: Flag update: `selector.fast_path_pref=0.6` applied to rollout/ksel-v2 at 1938001347. Rollout paused.

Maria: Traces started appearing consistently again after sampling bump + rollback. I can see full spans and the kernel-selection duration looks normal.

Alex: Perf profiles (pprof) from gpu-12-3 attached: main hotspots were `kv_cache:lookup` and `kernel:select_best` where select_best had a few outlier calls that took ~120ms each. Those correlate with cold cache misses.

Jane: After moving noisy tenant off gpu-12-3 and rebalancing, eviction rate dropped back to baseline. Throughput recovered slowly as cache warmed.

Sam: Action items: 1) Add a unit test to ensure kernel selector always emits a span even on fast-paths, 2) Make trace sampling bumpable via alert runbook, 3) Improve KV cache metrics export (per-tenant evictions). I'll open PRs for 1 and 3.

Alex: Thanks. Recording incident notes into the perf runbook. Marking postmortem follow-up: investigate scheduler backpressure that allowed noisy tenant to saturate GPU pool.

Priya: Final status: partial mitigation achieved at 1938001400, full stabilisation by 1938001440 after tenant move. Closing loop with customer success to confirm user impact. :white_check_mark:
